messages:
maria_k: heads-up — onboarding orion-v2 quantized to int8 shows a -2.3 BLEU delta on I18N-translate-v2 (zh->en) compared to fp16 baseline. repro + example below.

maria_k: quick sample that fails consistently: source contains mixed han+ascii numerals (e.g. "２０２３年 1,200 件"). output from int8 model drops the numeral or turns it into "1 200" spacing that breaks detok.

maria_k: repro command (can run on staging):
```bash
python eval.py --model orion-v2:int8 --dataset i18n-translate-v2 --split sample-1000 --batch 16 --detok-script detok_v2.py
```

maria_k: logs snippet shows token ids around the numeral changing: token ids for "1,200" vs "1 200": `[3245, 11, 4572]` -> `[3245, 256, 4572]` (256 is NBSP-like token).

jihoon: ugh. saw something similar last week with the new detok normalization mapping narrow NBSP -> token 256. Is this the int8 recompile or detok change?

alex: timeline: we merged qk_opt kernel v3 into runtime two days ago (commit 9f3b) and detok_v2.py normalization was updated by i18n eng yesterday (commit a12c).

maria_k: i ran the float baseline on the same exact detok_v2 and float is fine. so suspect interaction with quant path or kv-cache handling.

jihoon: can you run int8 with the older detok (detok_v1) quickly? if delta disappears it's detok. if not, probably runtime quant kernels.

maria_k: ran that — int8 + detok_v1 reduces delta to -0.6 BLEU (still present). int8 + detok_v2 = -2.3. float+detok_v2 = +0.0. so both matter but int8 amplifies it.

alex: can you try int8 with --no-kvcache (or set kvcache disabled) to rule out prefix caching weirdness?

maria_k: doing that now.

eval-bot: automated eval summary attached: 
- model: orion-v2:int8
- dataset: i18n-translate-v2/sample-1000
- metric: BLEU
- float baseline: 34.5
- int8 (detok_v2): 32.2
- int8 (detok_v1): 33.9
- int8 (detok_v2, no-kvcache): 33.7

maria_k: no-kvcache recovered most of it (33.7). so kvcache + detok_v2 + int8 = worst case.

jihoon: that points to a tokenization/tokenid consistency bug between serving runtime + kvcache and our detok normalizer. possibly kernel path returns token sequences with different whitespace normalization when quantized.

alex: @jihoon do you have a quick bisect plan? maybe run unit that compares tokenization outputs between fp16 path and int8 path with the exact same input bytes and the same tokenizer version.

jihoon: yes — create pairwise dump: run tokenization on input -> get token ids, run model to generate -> get token ids returned by step -> compare. suspect mismatch at runtime scatter for whitespace tokens.

maria_k: attaching two minimal examples that flip:
1) "２０２３年 1,200 件 は到着しました。" -> float: "In 2023, 1,200 items arrived." -> int8: "In 2023, 1 200 items arrived." (space inserted)
2) "請求額：￥１，２００" -> float OK, int8 breaks comma normalization

ops-bot: note: dedicated pool qk_opt v3 is rolled to canary; if we need to reproduce on dedicated let me know and I can pin commit. :wrench:

alex: plan: (1) jihoon to run token-id diffs and post small dump by EOD, (2) maria to run int8+no-kvcache across full dev set to confirm scope, (3) if reproduces, ops to roll back qk_opt v3 on canary to see impact.

jihoon: starting token-id diff now. quick preview: first 20 tokens around numeric area differ in representation (256 vs 11). dumping full JSON to /tmp/token-dump-1745006789.json

maria_k: thanks. i'll run the larger pass and post results here. if we confirm kvcache is the amplifier we might add a quick mitigation: detect narrow NBSP-class tokens pre-generation and map them to canonical space in the serving preprocessor for int8-only paths. ugly but buys time.

alex: agreed. long term we need parity tests that verify token-level roundtrips for every quantization profile during onboarding. filing a ticket after we confirm root cause.

jihoon: dump posted. sample diff: 
```
{"input":"...1,200...","float_ids":[3245,11,4572],"int8_ids":[3245,256,4572]}
{"token_map": {"256":"\\u00A0(narrow)"}}
```

maria_k: perfect — enough to triage. marking as high-priority internal regression. :exclamation:

ops-bot: Incident tracker ID: RINF-2026-0423 (internal). I'll schedule canary rollback window 30m if we need.

alex: nice catch. also note we should add this specific numeral+han sample to our regression prompt set. file i18n-translate-v2/regress/numeric-han-zwsp.txt

maria_k: adding that now. will update thread once larger run completes. :thumbsup:
